options.text: Fast air between the balloons lowers the pressure there, so higher pressure on the outer sides pushes P and Q together.
Fast air between the balloons raises the pressure there, so that higher pressure pushes P and Q apart.
The balloons move together even when the pressure between them equals the pressure on their outer sides.
The balloons move together because they look round, whether the air between them is moving or still.

stem:
The diagram shows two light balloons P and Q that Siddharth hangs a few centimetres apart. He blows a fast stream of air through the gap between them. The balloons move toward each other.

Which claim correctly decides how the fast-moving air changes the pressure?

teacher.key_rationale: High-speed air between the balloons lowers pressure there; higher outer pressure pushes them together. Reversing the pressure change, dropping the pressure difference, or judging from shape alone miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote force-arrow source into two balloons with fast air through the gap.
